page.title: Target
page.purpose: Explain one target completely: what was probed on which node, what it proved, which device-control strategy would drive it, and precisely what is missing when it is unavailable.

priorities.statement: A terminal target explains why it is terminal, and offers nothing to click.
priorities.notes: 'No Apple toolchain exists for Linux' is a complete answer. Suggesting a remedy would be false.

priorities.statement: Every probed capability is listed with its result and the time it was probed.
priorities.notes: Xcode version, simulator runtimes, GUI session, and signing identity each fail differently and each needs its own line.

priorities.statement: The driving strategy and its capability tier are named before a run, not only after.
priorities.notes: An operator should know they are about to get pixel-grade evidence before spending a run on it.

priorities.statement: Transport is explicit — local host or a named bridge node.
priorities.notes: The operator must be able to tell where work will actually execute, because that changes what can fail.

elements.name: Target disposition
elements.description: The closed-vocabulary disposition for this target, carrying a text label as well as a status colour.

elements.name: Probed capabilities
elements.description: One entry per probed prerequisite with its individual result.

elements.name: Probed at
elements.description: When the capability snapshot was taken.

elements.name: Missing capability
elements.description: The specific prerequisite that is absent, named rather than generalised.

elements.name: Next action
elements.description: The single action that would resolve this target's blocked state. Must not exist for a terminal target.

elements.name: Transport
elements.description: Local host or the named bridge node through which this target is reached.

elements.name: Driving strategy
elements.description: The device-control strategy that would drive this target and whether it is semantic or pixel-grade.

elements.name: Lease holder
elements.description: The consumer currently holding the device-control lease on this target, and since when.

states.description: A fully available simulator target on a macOS node.
The capability snapshot is being fetched; no results are asserted yet.
The target has never been probed. Explains that no snapshot exists rather than showing an empty capability list.
Some capabilities were probed and others could not be reached; the unprobed ones are explicitly unknown rather than assumed absent.
The capability snapshot is old enough that it may no longer hold. Age is shown prominently.
The probe request failed. Reported as a failure rather than as an unavailable target.
A native iOS target on the Linux host. Permanently unsupported, explained, with no remediation affordance.
The macOS node is online but has no logged-in GUI session, so the simulator cannot run. Distinct from a missing Xcode.
Xcode is present but the x86_64 universal simulator runtime variant is not installed on this Intel host.
A physical iPhone reachable through device-control. The xcuitest strategy is unavailable pending enrollment; the mirror strategy is available but pixel-grade.
The device is healthy and fully capable, but another consumer holds its device-control lease. Availability is a scheduling fact here, not a capability gap.

claims.statement: A target in the unsupported state presents an explanation and no action control.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. An affordance implies a path; there is none, and offering one wastes the operator's time on something structurally impossible while quietly destroying trust in every other disposition the UI reports.

claims.statement: Every unavailable target names both the missing capability and one next action.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. The counterpart promise: if terminal states must offer nothing, actionable states must always offer something specific.

claims.statement: A terminal target and a blocked-but-fixable target render distinguishably.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. These are semantically opposite answers and must not require reading the prose to tell apart.

claims.statement: Missing GUI session and missing simulator runtime variant render as different states on the same node.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. These fail for unrelated reasons; a single generic 'macOS node not ready' would make both undiagnosable.

claims.statement: Every capability result is accompanied by when it was probed.
claims.rationale: Capability is a measurement, and a measurement without a timestamp cannot be judged current.

claims.statement: Every reachable target names the transport through which work will execute.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-004. Where work runs changes what can fail, so it is part of reading the target.

claims.statement: A target names which strategy would drive it and whether that strategy is semantic or pixel-grade, before a run is started.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-002. Pixel-grade evidence is non-promotable; an operator must know that before spending a run rather than discovering it in review.

claims.statement: When one physical device offers both a semantic and a pixel-grade strategy, their differing availability and evidence tier are legible side by side before either is chosen.
claims.rationale: S2I-P1-001, S2I-P1-002. The iPhone is the only target with two strategies at different tiers, and choosing the wrong one wastes a run and produces evidence that cannot gate a release.

claims.statement: A target blocked by a held device-control lease names the holder and offers a next action rather than reporting a bare unavailable.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. A device is a single-occupancy resource. Without the holder named, contention is indistinguishable from a broken probe, and the operator goes looking for a fault that does not exist.

claims.statement: A target that is merely leased elsewhere renders distinguishably from one that is free and ready.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-005. A busy device becomes available by waiting; an incapable one never does. Collapsing them turns a queue into a phantom capability gap.
